originality.rationale: The exact source variational formula does not determine how many positive optimizing arguments exist. Section 7.2 states that the particular two-point example has an interior maximizer but explicitly leaves uniqueness unproved; the new theorem establishes strict unimodality on a parameter interval, an exact interior-to-origin threshold, and critical asymptotics. Primary comparisons with general compound-Poisson concentration and the M-class literature did not supply these statements or a stronger direct implication. Indexed research-record searches over uniqueness, equivalent exponential-MGF tangency, two-point jumps, and generalized equilibrium transforms yielded no covering finding. Residual risk of differently phrased or unindexed coverage is retained.

value.rationale: The motivating primary paper explicitly leaves uniqueness in its canonical two-jump interior example unresolved. A unique pole tangency ensures numerical optimal-scale determination is unambiguous; classifying an entire nontrivial mixture interval reveals a sharp transition to local-cumulant control with exact critical probability and onset exponents. The critical probability is a natural boundary in this concentration problem, not an arbitrary isolated parameter computation. The unclassified lower region is clearly delineated.
